messages:
sara: Heads-up — saw a customer hit a ton of 429s during a burst this morning. Metering shows the usage arriving ~45s later, but enforcer rejected the requests. Anyone else see this?

mike: Yeah, saw the spike around 09:12 UTC and the enforcer logs show a bunch of `reason=rate_limit` with no recent metering for those keys. Kafka consumer lag spiked at the same time.

jia: Quick dump from enforcer: we read last_synced_ts from memcache and compare to now; if too old we go into conservative throttle path. When pipeline lag > memcache window we start rejecting.

ben: Widening the memcache window is a short-term bandaid but ups the risk of unmetered consumption. We need something that absorbs short Kafka blips without breaking economics.

oliver: What if the metering pipeline emits a lightweight committed-watermark (compacted per-org topic) that enforcer subscribes to? Enforcer would allow requests up to watermark + burst_grace. Compacted topic reduces payload and keeps the latest committed offsets per org.

sara: Watermark + grace sounds reasonable. How do we handle rebalance/duplication so the enforcer doesn't read stale watermarks during a consumer restart?

mike: Use a compacted_kv topic keyed by org_id and persist a local checkpoint (partition+offset). The consumer is idempotent and we persist checkpoint in local RocksDB. That minimizes full re-syncs. Still, there may be a small lag during rebalance.

jia: Agreed. Combine that with a tiny local token pool per key (e.g., 30-100 tokens) that can absorb short interruptions. Tokens expire after N seconds. So: compacted watermark provides steady-state safety, local tokens cover transient blips.

ben: Also propose an hourly reconciliation job: compute enforcement vs metering delta and refund/annotate accounts that were over-throttled. Gives customer-facing recourse and helps debug patterns.

oliver: Operational note: don't just bump memcache TTL from 30s->90s. That hides the symptom. Heartbeat stream + token pool is safer.

sara: Action items: 1) prototype compacted watermark consumer and heartbeat topic (mike), 2) add local token pool fallback in enforcer (jia), 3) reconciliation job + dashboard delta metric (ben). Also add a console panel showing `enforcer_soft_allow` vs `hard_rejects` per-org.

mike: I'll spike the heartbeat compaction consumer + synthetic load test to model tail latency. Plan to measure: time-to-watermark after pipeline commit, and false-allow rate under rebalance.

jia: I'll add the token bucket fallback in enforcer with config knobs: token_count, token_ttl, and a toggle. Will add unit + e2e tests.

ben: I'll own the reconciliation runbook & dashboard. Dashboard should show: meter_ingest_lag, enforcer_rejections, allowed_from_local_tokens, and delta_refunds.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-4971, assigned to eng-platform, priority P2.

sara: Great. Please include rollback steps in each PR — e.g., toggle off token pool and fallback to strict enforcement. Let's sync 15:00 UTC to demo the spike test results.

mike: noted. I'll post a short demo GIF in the channel after the spike run. :thumbsup:

jia: One more thought — add a `ingest_watermark` header to metered requests going to enforcer in the future, so we can pass along causality info (experimental). Not blocking for the spike though.

ben: SGTM. Will prepare the reconciliation skeleton and a simple console mock by EOD.

sara: Thanks all — this should reduce customer-impacting false-429s while keeping billing accurate.
